title: Substance Abuse Counseling
tagline: Meeting young people inside the grip.
welcome: Adolescent substance use is rarely rebellion; it is usually relief. This course teaches you to meet the need beneath the use.
vignette: A fifteen-year-old vapes by the gate before school and drinks on weekends 'to quiet the noise.' He is not seeking help; he is seeking silence. The counselor's task is to offer a quieter, safer path than the substance.
vignette_attr: An adolescent substance-use intake, drawn from practice
description: A course in adolescent substance use and counseling: epidemiology and developmental impact, screening and assessment, motivational interviewing with young people, family-based interventions, relapse prevention, and recovery support in school and community.
questions: Why is this young person using, and what does it do for them?
How do I build motivation without confrontation?
How do I involve the family in recovery?
importance: Substance use reshapes the developing brain
Early skilled intervention changes the trajectory
Family involvement is the strongest predictor of youth recovery
misconceptions: that adolescents must hit rock bottom to change, when motivation can be built early
that confrontation works, when it typically increases resistance
figures: whose motivational interviewing changed the field
who co-developed the spirit and method of MI
whose family-based treatments lead youth outcomes
outcomes: Screen and assess youth substance use
You will use validated screening and developmental assessment.
You will evoke change talk with skill and spirit.
You will explain how substances shape the adolescent brain.
You will run family-based intervention elements.
You will prepare young people for high-risk moments.
You will link school, community, and peer recovery resources.
modules: Youth Substance Use: Scope and Development
Development explains both risk and hope.

tips: Roll with resistance; never wrestle it
Praise any change talk, however small

integration: Substance competence is essential for crisis, trauma, and school practice alike.
faith: We meet the young person with the same mercy we hope for, and a steadier path than the cup.
closing: May you offer a quieter relief than the substance, and may every young person find their way home to themselves.
